paper.title: Differentially Private Federated Combinatorial Bandits with Constraints

settings.name_in_paper: Federated CMAB in a homogeneous setting (with quality constraint)
unmapped: Procurement vectors: quantities l_ij in [0, k_ij] from each of the m producers; the expected revenue is sum_i l_ij (rho q_i - c_ij)
Constraint that the expected quality is at least a threshold alpha; rounds that violate it incur the maximal regret L
Homogeneous: costs and capacities are identical across agents, and qualities are shared
Agents share all observations every round (non-private)
The learner knows the costs, capacities and quality threshold alpha
The procurement set is chosen by a deterministic (approximation) Oracle
settings.definition_quote: We consider a combinatorial MAB (CMAB) setting where there are [m] producers and [n] agents. Each producer i has a cost c_ij and capacity k_ij for every agent j ... we characterize it as a Bernoulli random variable ... homogeneous: where the capacities and costs for producers are the same across agents

conditions: homogeneous costs and capacities across agents
bound is on the individual regret of each agent
tuning: agents communicate all observations every round
the UCB bonus is sqrt(3 ln(nt)/(2nW_i))

source.label: theorem:Homogenous Regret
source.quote: For Federated CMAB in a homogeneous setting with $n$ agents, if the qualities of producers satisfy $\gamma$-seperatedness, then the individual regret incurred by each of the agents is bounded by $\mathcal{O}(\frac{\ln (nT)}{n})$.

results.notes: The paper's n (number of agents) is mapped to N. Gap and constant factors (m, Delta_max, Delta_min, k) are hidden in the O; the proof gives an expression in these terms that contains typos. Regret is defined through expected revenue, so it is recorded as pseudo-regret.
